questions.question: A repository has a branch rule that requires one approving review before a pull request can be merged. A developer requests a review from Copilot, and Copilot completes its review. What is the result?

options.text: Copilot leaves a Comment review, and the pull request still needs one approval from a person
options.why: Correct. Copilot code review always leaves Comment reviews and does not count toward required approvals.

options.text: Copilot approves the pull request if it finds no problems, and the pull request can be merged
options.why: Copilot never submits an Approve review.

options.text: Copilot requests changes and blocks the merge until its comments are resolved
options.why: Copilot never submits a Request changes review.

options.text: Copilot merges the pull request after the status checks pass
options.why: Copilot code review does not merge pull requests.

questions.explanation: Copilot code review provides comments, often with suggested changes, but a required human approval is still needed.

questions.question: An organization wants Copilot to review every new pull request in its repositories without developers having to request the review manually. What should an administrator configure?

options.text: A ruleset that requests an automatic Copilot code review
options.why: Correct. A repository or organization ruleset can request a Copilot review on new pull requests automatically.

options.text: A .github/copilot-instructions.md file in each repository
options.why: Instructions define review standards. They do not request the review.

options.text: A CODEOWNERS file that lists Copilot for every path
options.why: Automatic Copilot reviews are configured through rulesets, not CODEOWNERS.

options.text: The Copilot coding agent policy set to Enabled
options.why: The coding agent works on assigned tasks. Enabling it does not review every pull request.

questions.explanation: Automatic Copilot code review is configured with a ruleset, after the Copilot code review policy is enabled.

questions.question: A team wants Copilot code review to flag any change to discount logic that does not include a unit test. What should the team do?

options.text: Add the rule to .github/copilot-instructions.md in the repository
options.why: Correct. Copilot code review uses repository custom instructions as review standards.

options.text: Add the rule to the pull request template
options.why: A pull request template pre-fills the description for authors. It is not where Copilot code review reads review standards.

options.text: Add the rule as a comment at the top of src/discount.js
options.why: A code comment is not a supported way to define review standards for every pull request.

options.text: Enable the suggestions matching public code policy
options.why: This policy controls public code matches. It does not define review rules.

questions.explanation: Customizable review standards are written in custom instruction files, which Copilot code review reads.

questions.question: Which TWO actions can a pull request author take on a Copilot code review comment that contains a suggested change?

options.text: Commit the suggested change directly from the comment
options.why: Correct. Suggested changes can be committed from the review comment.

options.text: Reply to the comment or resolve the conversation without applying the change
options.why: Correct. The author decides whether the suggestion fits and can reply or resolve it.

options.text: Convert the Copilot review into an approval
options.why: A Copilot review cannot be converted into an approval.

options.text: Mark the Copilot comment as satisfying a required reviewer
options.why: Copilot reviews do not count toward required approvals.

questions.explanation: Authors review each Copilot suggestion and either commit it or reply and resolve it. Copilot's review never acts as an approval.

questions.question: A developer wants Copilot to point out problems in local changes before pushing them to GitHub. What should the developer use?

options.text: Copilot code review from the IDE, on the selected code or the pending changes
options.why: Correct. Copilot code review can run in supported IDEs on code before it is pushed.

options.text: A Copilot pull request summary
options.why: A summary describes changes in a pull request. It does not review code for problems.

options.text: GitHub Spark
options.why: Spark builds micro apps from natural language. It does not review local changes.

options.text: The organization audit log
options.why: The audit log records administrative events, not code issues.

questions.explanation: Copilot code review is available on pull requests and in supported IDEs, so developers can get feedback before they push.
